description:
src/memory.rs:718-741 (node_matches_filter).

The function explicitly notes 'Only the filters used by integration tests are implemented: parentId, isTopLevel. All other fields are ignored (pass-through — node still matches).'

MemoryBackend is declared in PLAN.md and lib.rs as both an integration-test harness AND a 'reference impl' for downstream contributors to study. The 'silently pass through' default for the other FileNodeFilterCondition fields (ancestor_id, descendant_id, node_type, role, has_any_role, blob_id, type, name) makes the reference behavior wrong:

- A test that uses filter { 'role': 'inbox' } gets ALL nodes back, looking like a passing filter when in fact the filter was ignored.
- A downstream contributor reading the reference impl to understand FileNode/query semantics will copy the 'pass-through' shape into their real backend, introducing a security/data-leak bug (filter saying 'role=public' returns all roles).

Trigger for the test-oracle failure: any integration test that filters on a field other than parentId/isTopLevel. Bad behavior: test passes against MemoryBackend but the real query semantics are not exercised.

Trigger for the reference-impl footgun: a contributor adds a Postgres-backed FileNodeBackend, sees MemoryBackend treat unknown filter conditions as match-all, follows that shape. Result: filter evasion bug in the real impl.

Required: implement the missing conditions correctly (use the FileNodeFilterCondition fields from src/filter.rs:55-76: ancestor_id, descendant_id, node_type, role, has_any_role, blob_id, type, name). If selected conditions are genuinely out of scope, return Err on the unsupported condition rather than silently match-all.
title: MemoryBackend filter only matches parentId and isTopLevel; other conditions are silently passed through
